brief.headline: Cut ₹82,500 annual excess on measuring cups, move to 30-day payment to free ₹10.19 L cash, and qualify Manjushree or Mold-Tek as second source.

priceAsk.summary: Close the 8.6% gap on measuring cups to Premier Plastic's price and align to market fair-value at volume.
priceAsk.target: ₹0.35/NOS on MESU. CUP 30MM TRANS.PP 2.5/5/10ML (what Premier charges us) — saves ₹82,500 a year
priceAsk.basis: We pay Mars ₹0.38/NOS but Premier gives us ₹0.35/NOS for the same cup — an 8.6% gap. Market research shows similar PP caps (28 mm induction-wad) at ₹0.85–0.95/pc typical, with modest room down to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume or looser spec — verdict MARKET-FAIR. Our volume and the Premier benchmark justify closing the gap.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Move from 45 days to 30 days after receipt.
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Frees ₹10.19 L cash for us; another 15 days earlier frees another ₹5.10 L.

brief.financialLeverage: Mars Plastics publishes no financials, so we cannot see their profit, debt or how tight their cash is. Our ₹1.24 Cr annual spend is material to a private converter, but without their revenue we can't quantify our share. Because we lack visibility, the plan leans on our own purchase data (Premier's lower price, the ₹82,500 excess) and on lining up a robust second source — Manjushree (₹2569.83 Cr, health B 65/100) or Mold-Tek (₹1010.97 Cr, health B 73/100) — to create choice and anchor our ask in competitive reality.

evidence.point: We pay Mars 8.6% more than Premier on the same measuring cup.
Closing that gap saves us ₹82,500 a year.
Market research shows similar PP caps at ₹0.85–0.95/pc typical, with modest headroom down to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume — Mars's price is market-fair but not the floor.
evidence.figure: marketAsk typical ₹0.85–0.95/pc; modest headroom to ₹0.65–0.80; verdict MARKET-FAIR

evidence.point: Moving payment from 45 to 30 days frees ₹10.19 L cash for us.
Manjushree (India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter, ₹2569.83 Cr revenue, health B 65/100) is a top second-source candidate for pharma bottles and caps.
evidence.figure: Manjushree Technopack Ltd revenue ₹2569.83 Cr, health B (65/100)

evidence.point: Mold-Tek (listed, ₹1010.97 Cr revenue, health B 73/100) is a strong, profitable alternate for bottles and closures.
evidence.figure: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd revenue ₹1010.97 Cr, health B (73/100)

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter (₹2569.83 Cr, health B 65/100) with pharma bottles, caps and preforms — top second-source candidate.

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader (₹1010.97 Cr, health B 73/100) for pails, containers and pharma — strong, profitable alternate for bottles and closures.

risks: Mars publishes no financials — we cannot judge their cash position or how much squeeze they can handle; watch for signs of stress and keep the ask fair.
Premier's ₹0.35/NOS is our benchmark, but we buy only one SKU from Mars — if Mars walks, qualifying Manjushree or Mold-Tek will take time and audit cost.
Market backups (Reliance, Srichakra, IVL Dhunseri, Dalmia, Ganesha, Chemco) are leads to qualify — verify capability and price before issuing an RFQ; none are approved sources today.
Pushing too hard on both price and payment at once may spook a private supplier with no disclosed financials; sequence the asks or offer the faster payment in exchange for the price cut.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We value the partnership, and we'd like to close the 8.6% gap to what Premier charges us on measuring cups and explore faster payment terms — let's find a structure that works for both sides and keeps our volume with you.
